goal: Phase 2c (allowance-window-writers) of campaign adversarial-planner: the rate-limit window a sample measured reaches the seat.allowance journal event at both writers, so the cross-window guard protects a real delta instead of killing it. Supersedes node allowance-window-pinned of contract 2b, whose write scope excluded the two call sites. Spec: docs/campaigns/adversarial-planner/spec/SPEC.md.

definitionOfDone.text: allowance, campaign, field-ownership, plan and seat tests pass
both writers emit the window through the single helper, a same-window pair yields a real delta and a cross-window pair yields null with both windows visible

taskPacket.objective: The window a sample measured reaches the seat.allowance event at both writers (campaign init's start sample and plan freeze's freeze sample), the cross-window guard nulls only a genuine mismatch, and the previous attempt's confirmed work (window extraction from unifiedWindows, the adapter-built probe argv, the delta guard) stands.
instructions: The judge's verbatim finding on the previous attempt (contract 2b, node allowance-window-pinned): "What blocks the item is that the window never reaches a real journal event, and the new guard therefore kills the delta in production. `window` was added to ENTRY_SHAPES and to FIELD-OWNERSHIP, but neither writer of `seat.allowance` was changed: `campaign init` (src/cli/campaign.mjs:342) and `plan freeze` (src/plan/pipeline.mjs:236) still append the six old fields." Both call sites are in your write scope now. Everything else the judge confirmed must not change: extractClaudeAllowance reading the named window out of unifiedWindows with the top-level fallback, the adapter-built probe argv, the delta guard with its stated reason, the signal short-circuit as the first statement of normalizeClaudeResult, the out-of-range guard, the measured headers, ENTRY_SHAPES and the FIELD-OWNERSHIP declaration.

Read src/seat/allowance.mjs first: appendSeatAllowanceEvent (or whatever the single writer helper is called) is where the event object is built. Make it carry `window` from the sample, and make both call sites -- src/cli/campaign.mjs (the start sample at campaign init) and src/plan/pipeline.mjs (the freeze sample) -- pass the sample through that helper rather than assembling fields themselves. One writer, every field, both moments.

Tests, test/seat/allowance.test.mjs: a start sample and a freeze sample of the same window journal a delta and both events carry that window; a pair whose windows differ journals a null delta and both windows are visible in the events; the absent-signal path still records nulls without throwing. Add a case in test/campaign/campaign.test.mjs (or test/campaign/ledger.test.mjs, whichever already exercises campaign init's journal) asserting the init event carries the window field when a sample is available.
Keep the field-ownership ratchet truthful: appendSeatAllowanceEvent stays the single writer; if the two call sites currently appear as writers in the derivation, the refactor removes them from it.
decisions: A delta across two windows is not a delta: null, with the window on the record so a reader can see why.
The probe reuses the adapter's argv; no second command line for the same harness.
nonGoals: No change to what the judge already confirmed.
